clauses.control: Every mutation must match the complete live actor, workspace, subject, agent, installation, binding revision, connection and tenant tuple sealed by the Case.
The target reference must be server-issued, unexpired and resolve to the exact live target-session capability used by every ledger tool call.

requirements.business_risk: Write after delegation, kill-switch, target, policy or capability changed

clauses.control: Authorization is the intersection of live authority, capability, target and action; removal or mismatch of any dimension blocks before provider access.
Durable authority snapshot revision and hash are monotonic, and one revision may never identify different authority bytes.
The exact authority revision and hash are reread after preflight and immediately before the final write claim.

requirements.business_risk: Model changes payload, amount, action or tenant after prepare

clauses.control: The public execute schema accepts only case_id, case_version and request_id and rejects every client-supplied operation, action, tenant, provider or payload field.
Execute loads immutable operations only from the exact persisted Case version and rejects stale or cross-Case replay.

requirements.business_risk: False totals such as 800 plus 7.20 reported as 87.20

clauses.control: Every line and declared amount uses bounded fixed-decimal syntax and rejects floating-point, alternate-zero and excess-precision representations.
An independent source-to-canonical line and document bridge recomputes amounts and binds the result into source and operation hashes.

requirements.business_risk: Wrong tax, tax period, date, FX or economic readback

clauses.control: A versioned accounting-policy projection and the applicable document or original-transaction date uniquely determine supported tax periods and rates.
A live tax rate must resolve to exactly one active provider rate whose direction, numeric rate and account applicability all match the sealed policy.
Document, due and lock dates are canonical valid dates, and every date at or before an applicable lock boundary is blocked.
Every foreign-currency route requires typed supported FX evidence and the adapter may not omit or reinterpret the sealed rate.
Readback quantity, net, tax, account and tax type match the sealed policy projection for every line.
Readback document net, tax, gross, currency and aggregation match exactly, including a one-minor-unit adversarial difference.

A credit may reference a historical provider transaction only through server-resolved, exact-readback original-transaction evidence that is sealed and rechecked; the historical original is evidence-only and never compiled as a new write.

requirements.business_risk: Guessed or drifting contact, account, tax or provider route

clauses.control: Typed contact namespaces require external or durable registry authority; a provider bare-number match proves continuity only and never upgrades source truth.
The same exact verified contact tuple is idempotent, while a different unauthorised namespace tuple sharing a bare number is blocked before preparation, permit and create.
Every semantic account category resolves through one server-owned tenant, jurisdiction and revision profile to an exact live AccountID, code, type, class and configured semantics.
Every semantic tax key resolves to one live exact provider rate and is sealed and rechecked before the write claim.
One provider route and capability contract decides every action and bound; unsupported routes, shapes or bounds never fall back to another writer.

Contact identity collision discovery covers the complete provider lifecycle, including active, archived and privacy-erased or unknown states; only an exact active authoritative object may be reused and every inactive or incomplete result blocks create.

A legal contact identity is provider-role-neutral with a set of usage roles, so one verified entity shared by receivables and payables creates or reuses one provider contact and supplies every dependent document exactly once.

requirements.business_risk: Recognized source events disappear behind a completion claim

clauses.control: Source manifest, unit, fact and event identities and source bytes or revisions are frozen and included in the source hash.
Every expected fact and event has exact source-unit coverage and generic evidence cannot cover an unrelated set or collision.
Submitted-set completeness, write eligibility and residual disposition are independent dimensions and none may be inferred from another.

requirements.business_risk: Retry after timeout creates a duplicate provider object

clauses.control: Operation request identity is deterministically derived from the full server-owned Case, version, operation and action identity without collision.
The repository atomically grants one request owner; the same request is resumable and a different request conflicts.
A one-shot provider permit is durably consumed before any consumer call and remains consumed if the consumer throws or races.
Any possibly-sent or insufficiently-proven failure becomes write-uncertain and permits exact GET recovery only, never a second create.
Only a structured definite pre-write provider validation rejection may release a reservation as definitely failed.

Before preparation and again immediately before the provider write claim, a complete provider-history business-coordinate lookup returns NONE, EXACT_ONE, AMBIGUOUS or INCOMPLETE: NONE alone permits create; an EXACT_ONE object whose exact GET and canonical economic readback are identical yields NO_WRITE_REQUIRED_EXISTING without claiming a Case write receipt; every revised, mismatched, ambiguous or incomplete result is sealed and blocked without a provider write.

A submitted or model-extracted reference classification never grants a narrower duplicate scope: untrusted references reserve all occurrences, and dated recurring occurrences require a server-owned versioned recurring-series authority whose identity and occurrence key are sealed into the plan.

Each provider route has one server-authoritative business-coordinate projection that binds the trusted issuer, exact provider-persisted field, normalization and occurrence scope across all writer representations; mutable economic fields never define the coordinate, and a route whose authoritative field cannot be written and read exactly is blocked.

A provider route without a provider-enforced unique business coordinate permits autonomous create only under a server-verified exclusive governed-writer authority covering every tenant writer; absent that authority, the cross-system lookup-to-create race is blocked for manual review rather than represented as exactly-once.

requirements.business_risk: Provider accepted a write without durable object ID, receipt and exact readback

clauses.control: After provider create, only a durable exact provider object identifier and mutation receipt can advance recovery or success.
READBACK_VERIFIED requires the same provider object identifier and an exact canonical and economic projection.

requirements.business_risk: Evidence from different case, payload, target or authority is combined

clauses.control: The compiled-plan hash exactly binds access binding, Case, version and every compiled operation.
The preflight receipt exactly binds plan, binding, Case, version and every operation preparation, payload and source identity.
The durable preparation-to-mutation join requires the same owner, action, target, session, source and payload.
A provider permit is issued only from a hash-valid persisted authorization receipt and exact mutation request projection.
Mutation and readback evidence can update only the same Case operation and same provider object and receipt identity.

requirements.business_risk: Connection, permission and provider failures collapse into a misleading generic error

clauses.control: Every failure maps to a fixed layer, reason, recovery action and provider-mutation-possible classification, and post-send unknown never becomes safe retry.
The public failure envelope contains only allowlisted bounded fields and never provider bodies, secrets or arbitrary internal details.

requirements.business_risk: Credential-backed provider access occurs before the kernel write permit is consumed

clauses.control: An invalid, missing or consumed permit fails before provider client initialization.
An invalid, missing or consumed permit causes zero credential decryption, token-state or OAuth-refresh calls.
An invalid, missing or consumed permit causes zero provider network and SDK mutation calls, while a valid permit authorizes one exact adapter, action and payload.
A read-only provider client exposes no mutation-capable SDK method.
The production public tool allowlist exposes only the governed Case mutation choreography and no raw object or manual-journal writer.

requirements.business_risk: UAT exercises a stale toolset, policy, migration, authority state or unidentifiable worktree

clauses.control: Static attestation exactly binds release, toolset, kernel, compiler, policy, provider, validator and required migration head.
The acceptance snapshot captures every source path, byte, mode and hash once and detects worktree or snapshot mutation including mutate-and-restore.
Source archive, source manifest, bundle manifest and build identity are mechanically rebuilt from and match the immutable snapshot.
Every build stage and Dockerfile frontend is identified by an approved immutable digest rather than a mutable tag.
Buildx receives only one sealed deterministic context tar through stdin, never a second filesystem path read, and stdin failure is fatal.
The trusted verifier parses and hashes the OCI layout, manifest, config and every layer and rejects unsafe, duplicate, missing or extra archive entries and blobs.
OCI labels and embedded identity exactly equal the accepted source, archive, manifest and semantic build digests.
Readiness succeeds only when runtime build identity, repository schema and migration head and authority snapshot evidence all match.
Every production deployment path uses only the accepted repo-at-digest image, and cutover verifies RepoDigest, running image identity, labels and runtime readiness without rebuilding.
The Gate independently reconstructs the deterministic context identity and exactly matches every OCI receipt hash, size, count and source-manifest digest.

Release readiness and cutover fail while any active write-in-flight, write-uncertain or readback-mismatch Case uses a policy or provider projection that the candidate image cannot recover; compatible recovery must drain those Cases before the candidate becomes ready.

requirements.business_risk: Agent claims a write without a tool receipt and exact readback

clauses.control: Completion is mechanically derived from one durable Case, version and operation chain containing provider ID, mutation receipt and exact readback receipt.
Agent final output may repeat only the mechanical ledger claim and must never turn ledger readback into verified source truth.

requirements.business_risk: A release is declared locally acceptable after running only convenient checks or omitting product, architecture or evidence review

clauses.control: The Gate executes from a digest-named immutable snapshot and verifies source, inputs and mutation journals before, between and after every step.
The required deterministic suite set and order are fixed, and nonzero exit, collection error, timeout, overflow, skip or zero tests fail closed.
Canonical external control clauses exactly define all traceability claims and cannot be deleted or rewritten together with an implementation-authored summary.
The review universe is derived bottom-up from accepted release, runtime, deployment, migration, review tooling and fixed-baseline worktree state including additions and deletions.
Each atomic claim is partitioned into bounded semantic shards whose union covers every required vertex and dependency edge without omission.
Every review shard runs in a distinct fixed read-only approved Codex process whose executable, prompt, nonce and execution identity are replayable.
Every actual-content chunk is nonce, path, offset, size and hash bound and must be complete, ordered, untruncated and within encoded-output capacity.
Every probe obligation runs a fixed in-memory implementation mutation after a green baseline and must fail the specified collected assertion with zero skip or collection error.
Every cited positive and adversarial executable test is rerun by the Gate from current bytes with zero skip.
Each structured reviewer verdict reports all mandated review axes, concrete evidence, adversarial checks, rationale and residual risk; prose placeholders cannot close.
The aggregator requires the exact expected set of requirement, claim, shard and probe-obligation artifacts under one source, subject, universe, graph and partition identity.
Current local-Agent raw events and final output mechanically bind target choreography, writes, receipts, exact readback and source-truth boundaries.
Crash evidence uses real independent processes and current generator and source fingerprints at each governed crash boundary.
Redacted raw command, output, final, invocation and artifact bytes are individually hashed and any byte change invalidates closure.
The local Gate cannot self-close Gate L or substitute its own evidence for independent external approval.

requirements.business_risk: An ordinary business request cannot be converted into the strict Accounting Case contract without repeated schema guessing, or the convenience intake silently weakens authority and accounting controls

clauses.control: Business intake is a strict allowlist and rejects tenant, provider, operation, authority, payload, receipt and internal identifiers.
The same ordinary business input deterministically produces the same artifact, unit, fact and event identities independent of field order.
Every normalized intake output must pass the canonical public prepare schema before compilation.

requirements.business_risk: Xero, Singapore tax or chart-of-accounts assumptions are hard-coded into the shared control kernel and make the claimed solution provider-specific or unsafe to extend

clauses.control: Provider identity and accounting policy are separate injected contracts and a non-Xero provider and policy run the shared compiler without source changes.
The provider projection is sealed into source, plan and operation hashes and any provider binding or capability change invalidates the old plan.
The policy projection is independently sealed into source, plan and operation hashes and policy change invalidates the old plan.
The shared transitive dependency closure contains no Xero, Singapore, tax-code, tax-rate or tenant chart literal or provider import.
Provider route and capability bounds are interpreted only by the injected adapter contract and the shared kernel has no provider-specific fallback.

requirements.business_risk: A valid currency amount is rejected, rounded inconsistently, or read back against a different line/document rounding rule

clauses.control: Every currency resolves through a versioned policy minor scale and unsupported currencies fail closed.
The policy selects one integer rounding mode and no floating-point or implicit provider rounding is used.
Tax aggregation follows the sealed per-line rule and document-total rounding cannot replace line aggregation.
Compiler, service preparation and readback use the same sealed quantizer, scale and aggregation rule.
Monetary rule version, scale, mode and aggregation are fully included in policy, source and plan identities and old rules are never silently reinterpreted.
